authority_basis.claim_scope: A free-body diagram shows only forces acting on the selected body/system.

concepts.statement: The body or system must be selected before deciding which forces belong on its free-body diagram.
concepts.why_required: An FBD is defined relative to one selected receiver/system boundary.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Forces on different bodies, or both members of an interaction pair, can be mixed onto one diagram.

model_conditions.condition: Exactly one body or explicitly declared multi-body system is selected before the FBD is constructed.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Only external interactions crossing that boundary belong on the diagram.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The diagram can contain forces acting on other receivers or omit forces acting on the selected system.

representations.semantic_geometry: The selected body or system is isolated and every external force acting on it is drawn as a directed arrow with physical identity.
must_not_imply: forces exerted by the selected body belong on its FBD
motion direction itself creates a force
representations.verification_method: Cross-check every arrow against the interaction map and verify the arrow acts on the selected receiver.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Select one body or explicitly defined system before drawing forces.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The diagram has no unambiguous receiver boundary.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify all external interactions crossing the selected boundary.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A real force may be omitted or an internal force may be included.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Draw only forces acting on the selected system, with correct directions and physical identities.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The force model remains verbal and cannot safely feed Newton equations.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Check every arrow has a physical agent and receiver consistent with the chosen system.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Third-law pairs or fictitious motion forces can remain undetected.

required_transformations.description: Isolate the body or system whose dynamics will be modelled.
Translate each external interaction into exactly one justified force arrow on the selected receiver.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Both members of a Newton third-law pair belong on one body's free-body diagram.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Equal-and-opposite pair language is often learned before receiver identity is secure.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: For a book on a table, the table-on-book normal appears on the book FBD while the book-on-table force acts on the table and belongs on the table FBD.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Draw two separate receiver-labelled FBDs for the two bodies.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: An FBD contains forces on the selected body only; the partner force acts on the other body.
misconceptions.verification: For every arrow, identify the receiver and reject arrows whose receiver lies outside the selected system.

problem_families.name: Construct a free-body diagram
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the receiver/system boundary before listing forces.

problem_families.name: Diagnose an incorrect free-body diagram
recognition_cues: candidate diagram with extra or missing arrows
problem_families.first_technical_move: Audit each arrow by agent, receiver and interaction crossing the boundary.
fatal_errors: accepting action-reaction partners on one FBD

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove selected-system-first semantics from the FBD gate.
